newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court dismisses Spain's challenge to Commission aid decision.
newsitem.headline: Court dismisses Spain's challenge to Commission aid decision.

text.p: The European Court of Justice dismissed on Thursday a challenge from Spain to the European Commission's decision that aid given to the Piezas y Rodajes steel foundry in Spain was illegal.
After first approving the regional aid in 1987, the Commission reversed its decision in 1997, declared the aid unlawful and ordered repayment with interest.
The Commission originally approved the aid because the steel foundry was located in an area needing economic development assistance.
In 1991, the British steel prodcing company, William Cook plc challenged the compatibility of the aid with the common market and the Commission opened an investigaton with the Spanish authorities.

The Commission upheld the aid and Cook sought and won annulment of the Commission decision before the European court, in so far as the decision related to aids other than the original PTA 975,905,000 subsidy from Spain to Pieas.

The court told the Commission it should have initiated the procedure under article 93(2) of the Treaty to see if the aid were compatible with the common market, and not based its decision on a lack of overcapacity in the sprockets and GET parts sub-sector.
Following that court ruling, the Commission adopted its decision, contested in this case, that the aid to the steel foundry was illegal.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Spanish)
Commission of the European Communities, defendant

application for annulment of Commission decision 95/438/EC of 14 March 1995 concerning investment aid granted by Spain to the company Piezas y Rodajes SA, a steel foundry located in Teruel province (Aragon) Spain (OJ 1995 L 257, p. 45)
2. Orders the Kingdom of Spain to pay the costs.
